analysis.investment_thesis: KRN trades at 116x earnings and 14.9x book value — roughly 10x my Graham Number of ~₹128 — offering precisely zero margin of safety. Despite admirable operating growth, the price demands perfection and embeds decades of future earnings that have not yet been proven.
key_strengths: Low financial leverage: D/E of just 0.06 and debt down from ₹87 Cr to ₹33 Cr
Consistent profit growth: Net profit CAGR of 71% (₹11 Cr → ₹53 Cr, 2022–2025)
Operating CF positive all 4 years, with ROCE of 20.8% indicating decent capital deployment
key_risks: Extreme valuation: P/E 116x vs my maximum of 15x; P/B 14.9x vs my maximum of 1.5x
Persistently negative free cash flow: FCF was -₹9, -₹41, -₹65 Cr over 2023–2025 despite book profits
Capital-intensive expansion eating cash: capex of ₹151 Cr in FY25 funded almost entirely by IPO proceeds (financing CF +₹258 Cr)
red_flags: Graham Number ≈ ₹128; stock trades at ₹1,270 — a 10x premium over intrinsic value by my method
Incorporated 2017, listed 2023 — a recent IPO lacking the 5-year earnings track record I require
Equity tripled (₹130 Cr → ₹528 Cr) via IPO capital raise — investment bankers priced this for sellers, not buyers
No dividend — zero cash returned to shareholders; all earnings are reinvested under assumptions of future growth
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By every quantitative test I apply, KRN is disqualifying. My Graham Number — derived from ₹8.54 EPS and ₹85 book value per share — yields roughly ₹128, against a market price of ₹1,270. The stock must decline 90% before I would consider it statistically cheap. P/E of 116x is nearly eight times my ceiling of 15x; P/B of 14.93x is ten times my ceiling of 1.5x. The market is pricing in many years of flawless 40–70% growth, and the intelligent investor does not pay for what has not yet occurred.

The balance sheet shows one genuine virtue — negligible debt — but the cash flow statement is troubling. Operating cash flow of ₹21 Cr in FY25 is dwarfed by ₹151 Cr of capex, producing -₹65 Cr of free cash flow. The equity surge from ₹130 Cr to ₹528 Cr reflects IPO proceeds, not retained earnings. This is a young company (incorporated 2017) in rapid, capital-hungry expansion, financed by public shareholders who have been handed an optically impressive growth story at an extreme price. Mr. Market is euphoric about this company today; the disciplined investor waits for the day Mr. Market despairs.
